title: Temporal Decomposition of Transaction Sequencing (Manual Flushes)
pattern: Core business calculations manually managing database transaction boundaries, flushes, or commit ordering.
why_bad: It couples business logic to database-specific transaction flow constraints, leading to fragile core code that easily triggers constraint violations during simple refactorings.
detection: Function bodies in domain packages containing direct calls to transaction control APIs (like `.flush()`, `.commit()`, or `.start_transaction()`).
counterexample: Low-level integration tests asserting database boundary states. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Move transaction-sequencing control entirely into a separate Unit of Work or infrastructure-level interceptor wrapper.
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* by Martin Fowler (p. 184, "Unit of Work").
